==Problem== Casey's shop class is making a golf trophy. He has to paint 300 dimples on a golf ball. If it takes him 2 seconds to paint one dimple, how many minutes will it take for him to finish \mathrm{(A) \ 4 } \qquad \mathrm{(B) \ 6 } \qquad \mathrm{(C) \ 8 } \qquad \mathrm{(D) \ 10 } \qquad \mathrm{(E) \ 12 } ==Solution== It will take him 300\cdot2=600 seconds to paint all the dimples. This is equivalent to \frac{600}{60}=10 minutes \Rightarrow \boxed{D}. ==See Also== {{AMC8 box|year=2001 |before=First
Question|num-a=2}} [[Category:Introductory Algebra Problems]] {{MAA Notice}}
